title: Spanlet annotation mini-protocol (scratchpad)
body:
Quick scratchpad of a tiny "spanlet" annotation protocol we can push into client proxies / edge adapters. Goal: extremely compact, append-friendly, and friendly for partial decoding during ingest so downstream pipelines can make routing/aggregation decisions without full decode.

Summary:
- Spanlet = minimal span-like tuple attached to request/response fragments. Designed for: edge adapters, mobile SDK proxies, L7 sidecars.
- Key constraints: <= 64 bytes on average, ASCII-safe header or short binary blob, easy to map to existing trace IDs, optional structured tags.
- Use-cases: latency SLO bucketing at ingress, quick error tagging for sampling, shard-aware routing in prefetched KV caches, local aggregation for warmup heuristics.

Design goals / constraints (raw):
- Shortness: header-friendly (HTTP header value or small POST body)
- Backwards compatibility: allow passthrough if not recognized (ignore unknown versions)
- Partial decoding: first 16 bytes give enough to route -> e.g., model family shard, tenant id hash, severity hint
- Privacy: no PII, hashed/opaque tenant IDs only

Protocol sketch (human readable):
- Carrier: HTTP header X-Spanlet or binary attribute in gRPC metadata. If header length > 160 bytes, split into multiple spanlet segments with sequence numbers (spanlet-1/2...).
- Format v1: human-friendly token format: <ver>|<tid-32bhex>|<m>|<s>|<k-v-list-base64>
  - ver: 1 (single ascii digit)
  - tid: 16-byte trace-id hex (we accept short form, first 16 hex chars)
  - m: model-family short code (3-6 chars, e.g., 'gptj','rwrf')
  - s: severity hint / priority (0-7) used by routing / sampling
  - k-v-list-base64: optional small key-value compressed payload (gzipped protobuf-lite and base64)

Example header v1 (text):
X-Spanlet: 1|4f3ac2b9a1d4e7c3|rwrf|2|QmFzZTY0VlZQ (note: last part is example base64)

Compact binary variant (v1b):
- Byte layout (12 bytes minimum):
  0: version (1 byte)
  1-8: tid_hash (64-bit little-endian) -- first 8 bytes of trace id hash
  9: model_code_idx (1 byte) -- index into model code table per process
  10: severity (3 bits) + flags (5 bits)
  11: payload_len (8-bit) if small (<=255) else 0xFF then 16-bit len follows
  follow: payload bytes (compressed k-v)

Model code table (process-local): small mapping to keep spanlet tiny. Example entries: 0->unknown, 1->rwrf, 2->l2-medium, 3->gptj, 4->embed-32

Payload encoding (k-v list): very small TLV: 
- Repeated entries: <klen:1><kbytes><vlen:1><vbytes> ... (klen/vlen each 1 byte)
- Keys are short tags (3-8 ascii chars). Values typically small numbers or short ascii. For anything bigger we fall back to compressed base64.

Example compact tuple (binary hex):
01 9a 7f 4c 21 12 ff 0a 03 42 05 74 03 31 33 2e
- decode: v1, tid_hash=0x0aff12214c7f9a01, model idx 3=>'gptj', severity 2, payload len 5, payload= 't\x0313.' (toy)

Ingress processing semantics:
- If spanlet present and decodable: increment per-model ingress counters (fast path)
- If payload contains sample_hint=1: route to higher fidelity trace capture and set trace sampling to 100% for this request
- If model_idx unknown: use model_code 'unknown' and record at low cardinality metric

De-dup / idempotency rules:
- Multiple spanlet headers: take first valid one unless seq header indicates ordering. This keeps header parsing O(1).
- For chunked streams: allow spanlet segments with seq numbers, reassemble only if aggregator needs expanded key-values. Most consumers will use only first segment.

Mapping to existing tracing:
- We reuse the trace-id (short) field when available so spanlets can be joined to traces later. For private tenants, we prefer tenant-hash instead of raw tenant id.
- If both traceparent and spanlet exist, spanlet is used for ingress heuristics, traceparent for full trace correlate.

Privacy & security notes:
- Never include user-visible strings. Key-values restricted to pre-approved keys (config map).
- Payload compressed with zlib and then base64 when carried in textual header to avoid injection problems.
- Consider HMAC signature for spanlet in high-trust deployments to prevent spoofing (extra flag + 8-byte suffix). HMAC key rotates by region.

Operational considerations:
- Version negotiation: header starting with digit. Unknown version -> ignore. Version bumping strategy: v2 moves to TLV-first format to allow richer tagging.
- Migration: start with passive parsing in edge adapters, emit metrics on how many spanlets successfully parsed and unknown model_idx counts.
- Sampling: default low-fidelity path: only severity>=5 triggers downstream full trace capture. Configurable per-tenant.

ASCII diagram (rough):
Client SDK / Sidecar -> [X-Spanlet header] -> Edge Proxy -> Spanlet FastPath -> route to model shard / sampling -> telemetry counters
                                                    
If >payload threshold -> send full k-v to ingestion service (async)

Open questions / TODO (short):
- exact model_code table distribution: process local vs global registry? tradeoffs: local <= tiny header vs global index management.
- should tid be full 16-byte trace-id or 8-byte hash? 8-byte smaller but increases collision chance; acceptable for routing heuristics?
- what keys are safe for clients to emit by default? propose whitelist: {env, region, sample_hint, tenant_hash, feature_flag}
- implement prototype parser in go + rust and measure median header parse time (goal <150ns)
- define retention and downstream schema mapping for k-v keys to metrics/tags

Notes-to-self (implementation steps):
1) write go parser that accepts both text and binary v1 variants. add unit tests for malformed headers.
2) wire passive metric emission in edge-proxy: spanlet.parsed_total, spanlet.parse_errors, spanlet.unknown_model_idx
3) add CLI tool spanlet-encode for debugging (encode sample k-v)
4) experiment with 8 vs 16 byte tid: run synthetic collision test over 1B random ids

Quick sample k-v textual payload examples (human):
- sample_hint=1;tenant_hash=8f3a;env=prod;region=us-west1
- feature_flag=short_warmup;prefetch=true

Rough performance targets (ballpark):
- header parse latency < 200ns (fast-path inline C/Go)
- common spanlet size in header < 48 bytes (including base64)
- false-positive routing (due to hash collisions) < 1e-6 at 1M rps

Back-of-envelope encoding cost:
- textual v1: ~32-80 bytes typical (base64 payload only when needed)
- binary v1b: 12-40 bytes typical (good for high-throughput internal lanes)

Misc brainstorming notes (short bullets):
- could reuse JWT-like compactness? probably heavy. Keep it tiny.
- consider protobuf-lite compress + brotli for longer payloads but avoid on hot path.
- allow adapter-local caching of model_idx->route to replace full lookup table for speed

End of scratchpad.

-- avery
